test_title: SSC Selection Post 2025 (Higher Secondary Level) Official Paper (Held On: 31 July, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
A sentence is provided in indirect speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding direct speech.

Rita said that she could not attend the meeting because she was unwell.

options.text: Rita said, "I cannot attend the meeting because I am unwell."
Rita said, "I will not attend the meeting because I was unwell."
Rita said, "I could not attend the meeting because I was unwell."
Rita said, "She could not attend the meeting because she was unwell."

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** Rita said that she could not attend the meeting because she was unwell.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"she could not attend" becomes "I could not attend"**
 
 
• Pronoun "she" is changed to "I" to match direct speech.
 
• Verb "could" remains unchanged as it retains the past tense.
 
 
 
• **"because she was unwell" remains "because I was unwell"**
 
 
• Pronoun "she" is converted to "I" for direct speech.
 
 
 
• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• Indirect: "said"
 
• Remains "said" in direct speech, as there is no change in tone or context.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• Starts with a capital letter "I" and ends with a full stop ".".
 
• Reporting clause follows the quoted speech, starting with a lowercase letter after the comma.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"“I could not attend the meeting because I was unwell,” said Rita."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "I cannot attend the meeting because I am unwell," said Rita."
 
 
• Incorrect tense: "cannot" and "am unwell" change the meaning from past inability to present inability.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** "I will not attend the meeting because I was unwell," said Rita."
 
 
• Incorrect tense: "will not attend" changes the meaning to a future decision rather than a past event.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "She could not attend the meeting because she was unwell," said Rita."
 
 
• Incorrect pronoun: "she" does not match the direct speech format where Rita speaks about herself.
